newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-BELEAGUERED SACCHI SHUNS CONTROVERSY BEFORE BOSNIA GAME.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-BELEAGUERED SACCHI SHUNS CONTROVERSY BEFORE BOSNIA GAME.

text.p: Italy's highly-symbolic soccer friendly against Bosnia in Sarajevo on Wednesday looks at first glance to be the perfect match for Arrigo Sacchi.
The beleaguered Italy coach has no crucial World Cup qualifying points at stake, nobody is challenging his tactics or team and, best of all, the key word is goodwill.
The game at the Kosevo stadium will be the first international soccer match played in the Bosnian capital since a war that turned some pitches into graveyards.
The last time Sacchi's team appeared in Italy, they were whistled and booed by the disappointed crowd.
In Sarajevo, a city whose inhabitants were bombed and besieged during more than four years of suffering, Italy's arrival will be a celebration.
A turnout of around 50,000 is expected at the game, played in the afternoon because of a lack of floodlights.

"It's clear that there is another reason for going to Bosnia," Sacchi told reporters on Tuesday. "It's about happiness and being able to help these people return to normality as soon as possible. We want to do something good for them."
But Sacchi, despite calling for controversy to be put aside, will not be lowering his guard.
The match will be Italy's last before they travel to England for a crucial World Cup qualifier at Wembley in February and few would bet on Sacchi being there.
Italian soccer officials have hinted that when a new federation head is elected next month, Sacchi's contract -- which currently runs to 1998 -- could be terminated.
The match in Bosnia could be his last at the helm.
"I don't know what my future is. I don't think anyone does," he said on Tuesday, adding that he believed contracts were to be respected.
Former federation chief Antonio Matarrese, who made the original promise to play in Sarajevo, lost his job after this year's European championship.

He will not be travelling to Bosnia due to a FIFA meeting in Zurich this week when one of the items on the agenda will be whether the Kosevo stadium is safe for international matches. Bosnia currently play their matches in Italy.
Sacchi said Italy was taking the match seriously. "I think even the Bosnians would take it badly if we did not go to play seriously," he said.

His team has been depleted because the top three clubs in the league -- Inter, Vicenza and Juventus -- have Italian Cup replays on Wednesday and only suspended Juventus defender Moreno Torricelli is available to travel.
Milan defender Alessandro Costacurta pulled out with a knee injury and Parma's Luigi Apolloni takes his place.

Middlesbrough striker Fabrizio Ravanelli and Chelsea midfielder Roberto Di Matteo have been summoned from England along with two provincial newcomers and several old faces. Sacchi has now called up 93 players since he became coach.
Fiorentina defender Pasquale Padalino and Perugia midfielder Federico Giunti are the newcomers.
Atalanta's Gianluigi Lentini, the world's most expensive player when he joined Milan in 1992, gets his chance of a first cap since a near-fatal car crash in 1993.
Given the nature of the match, all 18 players are expected to appear on the field at some point.
Italy squad:
Goalkeepers: Francesco Toldo, Luca Marchegiani.
Defenders: Daniele Carnasciali, Moreno Torricelli, Alessandro Nesta, Luigi Apolloni, Pasquale Padalino, Paolo Maldini.
Midfielders: Dino Baggio, Gianluigi Lentini, Roberto Di Matteo, Demetrio Albertini, Federico Giunti.
Forwards: Gianfranco Zola, Pierluigi Casiraghi, Fabrizio Ravanelli, Enrico Chiesa, Marco Simone.
